content: Hydrangea arborescens, commonly referred to as Wild Hydrangea or Smooth Hydrangea, is a species of Hydrangea that is indigenous to the eastern regions of North America. The cultivar known as Annabelle is the most widely recognized variety of this species. It is notable for being one of the most cold-hardy Hydrangeas, capable of withstanding lower temperatures compared to other species. Another cultivar, Grandiflora, produces flowers that bear a striking resemblance to snowballs, similar in appearance to those of Viburnum plicatum. This particular variety is often referred to as the Hills-of-Snow Hydrangea.
